overview: Rise 6.1.30's Regen is a ModeValue shell registering three heal-forcing modes (Vanilla, Verus Regen, World Guard), each gated on a Minimum Health setting that defaults to 15. Every mode reacts to the PreMotion event while the health bar is below the gate and floods the C03 channel with position packets that re-assert the current position. On a stock 1.8.9 server this cannot accelerate natural regeneration: FoodStats.onUpdate heals 1 HP per 80 ticks while foodLevel is at least 18, called once per tick from EntityPlayer.onUpdate, and no serverbound packet touches that timer. The module's observable effects are therefore the packet rate (roughly 400 to 600 packets per second depending on the mode), the onGround flags attached to the burst, and in the World Guard mode a grounded-attack sandwich that rewrites the C02 attack stream.

sections.p: The shell holds a single ModeValue with three modes under com/alan/clients/module/impl/combat/regen/: VanillaRegen (default), VerusRegen and WorldGuardRegen. Each mode declares its own Minimum Health NumberValue (1 to 20, default 15) and its own PreMotion listener; there is no shared packet loop in the shell itself. The mode classes are the entire mechanism, which makes the default mode class the natural supporting file for the full-source page.

VanillaRegen sends the packet Speed value (1 to 100, default 20) C06PacketPlayerPosLook packets per tick while health is below the gate, each carrying the real position, real yaw and pitch, and the real onGround flag: 20 packets per tick is roughly 400 per second of zero-distance position claims. VerusRegen sends 30 C04PacketPlayerPosition packets per tick with onGround hard-coded true, but only while the local player is actually on the ground, so the burst is roughly 600 per second of identical grounded claims. Because every packet re-asserts the identical coordinate, the server-side physics envelope sees zero-distance moves; the only server-visible signal is the rate at which the C03 channel is consumed.

sections.h: World Guard mode and the vanilla regen ceiling
sections.p: WorldGuardRegen is a combat-side variant. While grounded and below the health gate, the first tick of the burst drops the sent y by 0.05 in PreMotion, freezes yaw and pitch, cancels every C02 attack and re-sends it sandwiched between a C04PacketPlayerPosition(pos, onGround true) and a C04PacketPlayerPosition(pos, y minus 0.05, onGround false), cancels incoming S2D open-window packets, and zeroes strafe speed and jump input. The attack therefore reaches the server while the claimed body sits grounded at the original y. None of this changes the regen ceiling: natural 1.8.9 regeneration is 1 HP per 80 ticks from FoodStats.onUpdate, and a stock server never re-evaluates healing from move packets, so the module only matters against forks or plugins that heal per movement.

files.label: Regen.java (mode selector)
files.explanation: The ModeValue shell that registers the three modes. It contains no packet logic: mode dispatch happens through the shared ModeValue chain and each mode class binds its own PreMotion listener. The shell's only member is the ModeValue declaration with Vanilla set as the default. Reading the shell alone yields nothing about the wire behavior, which is why the full-source page embeds the default mode class next to it.

files.label: VanillaRegen.java (default mode)
files.explanation: The default mode and the wire fingerprint of the module. Its PreMotion listener compares the local health bar against the Minimum Health gate and, when below it, sends the Speed value (default 20) C06PacketPlayerPosLook packets per tick through PacketUtil.send, roughly 400 packets per second of identical position claims. The C06 variant is the full position-plus-rotation claim, so each packet carries 3 doubles plus yaw, pitch and the onGround byte. The VerusRegen sibling pushes 30 C04PacketPlayerPosition packets per tick with a hard-coded grounded flag, gated on the local player actually touching ground.

countering.label: FastHeal (regen cadence)
countering.explanation: The decisive counter and the only check that nullifies the module's output. NoCheatPlus hooks EntityRegainHealthEvent at LOW priority through FightListener.onEntityRegainHealthLow and applies the fast-heal model to heals whose RegainReason is SATIATED, which is exactly the natural hunger-regen path the module exists to accelerate. Heals arriving closer than fastHealInterval (default 4000ms, DefaultConfig FIGHT_FASTHEAL_INTERVAL) drain a buffer of fastHealBuffer (default 1000ms); the violation level accumulates with 0.96 decay and the default actions cancel the regain event outright once the level passes 10, escalating to a kick command. The check is packet-agnostic: it watches the Bukkit heal event, so the 400 to 600 packet per second C03/C04 floods never reach it and never help. On a server running NoCheatPlus the module's entire output, a heal attempt beyond the natural 4-second cadence, is cancelled before it lands.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation: MorePackets counts the raw rate of serverbound move packets regardless of content. MovingListener invokes morePackets.check on every processed move (line 1561), each scored into data.morePacketsFreq, an ActionFrequency with 500ms buckets (MovingData line 321), and NetStatic.morePacketsCheck accumulates the window score against cc.morePacketsEPSMax, default 22 packets per second with 20 ideal, plus a burst path on the newest half-second bucket (default 15 packets, direct-violation 10, burst events 95 per minute) with lag adaption via TickTask. VanillaRegen at 20 C06 packets per tick sustains roughly 400 per second and VerusRegen roughly 600, both near 20 times the window ceiling, so the window accumulator runs positive for the whole window and the epsacc tag cancels at vl above 2 under the default actions. The zero-distance nature of the claims is irrelevant: the check scores every packet, including the identical re-assertions.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly rebuilds the physics envelope from the world instead of trusting the packets. The horizontal allowance comes from prepareSpeedEstimation and the vertical from vDistRel (line 1839), and the violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) plus max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) times 100 (line 233), with handleViolation set-backs to the stored location. The regen floods re-assert the identical position, so the per-move deltas are zero and the envelope itself passes: this is an honest boundary, not a hit. What the check contributes is ground truth and the set-back anchor: fromOnGround and toOnGround come from RichBoundsLocation.isOnGround(), which scans the actual block cache at minY minus yOnGround, never the packet flag, and MorePackets seeds its set-back from the SurvivalFly location when one exists. Any mode that ever claims a grounded flag over air, the classic regen collision-gate race, is caught by the block cache here.

countering.label: NoFall (faked onGround)
countering.explanation: NoCheatPlus tracks fall distance itself from the server-side y coordinates and deals the accumulated damage on ground contact, so a client that claims onGround early does not reset the ledger. The violation path requires the client's claimed landing to contradict the server-computed fall state. None of the Rise regen modes present that lie: VanillaRegen forwards the real onGround flag, VerusRegen only bursts while the local player is genuinely on the ground, and WorldGuardRegen's onGround-false claim rides a 0.05 y drop that stays far under any fall-damage threshold. The entry is an honest boundary: the check that catches classic regen ground-spoofers never arms against this module because the modes gate their claims on actual ground state.
